requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
The marked tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.fingerprints`.

**Comments are excluded.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a TOML case that selects `table[t]`. It covers a standalone comment and a trailing comment.
- Editing the comment text leaves the hash unchanged, and so does removing the comments.
- Changing the non-comment value (`a = 1` to `a = 2`) changes the hash, so the test does not pass just because the hash ignores everything.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` also has a TOML case. Changing `# note` to `# edited` leaves the hash unchanged.

**Whitespace-separated words, with no hashing of whitespace.**
- The same TOML case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` changes `"two words"` to `"two   words"` and expects the same hash.
- It changes `"two words"` to `"twowords"` and expects a different hash. That checks that word boundaries are encoded.

**SHA-256.**
- The same test asserts that each hash is 64 hex digits.
- That check alone would accept any 64-hex digest. The exact algorithm is covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. It checks the standard SHA-256 empty vector and a tagged, length-prefixed token digest. It tests the shared `Encoder`, which the structural-hash requirement says applies in every language.

**Fingerprint scheme.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` and its helper `fn[check]` assert that `languages::Toml` reports the scheme `toml-structural-v1`.
- They also assert that the scheme is the same for the default instance, and that a file inferred from a `.TOML` path (`a.TOML`) retains it.
- Scheme retention by loaded contents is the job of the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`. I did not reassess it here.

The two cited requirements, `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, are context. I did not reassess them.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
